title: Your first image: checkpoint, sampler, VAE

questions.q: Which three networks does Load Checkpoint hand to the rest of an SD 1.x graph?
options: The sampler, the scheduler and the VAE
The denoiser (a UNet), the text encoder (CLIP) and the VAE
Two text encoders and a UNet
The denoiser, the VAE and an upscaler
questions.answer: The denoiser (a UNet), the text encoder (CLIP) and the VAE
questions.why: CheckpointLoaderSimple returns MODEL, CLIP and VAE. The sampler is not a network but the loop that calls the denoiser, and its schedule is a list of numbers.

questions.q: For a 512 by 512 image the lab compares what the sampler works on with the picture. What does it find?
options: 786,432 numbers for the sampler against 16,384 for the picture
16,384 numbers for the sampler against 786,432 for the picture, 48 times more in the picture
The same number for both
65,536 numbers for the sampler against 3,145,728 for the picture
questions.answer: 16,384 numbers for the sampler against 786,432 for the picture, 48 times more in the picture
questions.why: The latent is [1, 4, 64, 64], which is 16,384 numbers. The IMAGE is [1, 512, 512, 3], which is 786,432. The ratio is 48, as CU-103 found for every size.

questions.q: With 20 steps and denoise 0.5, what is the first sigma in the lab, and why?
options: 7.3073, half of the first sigma of the full list
14.6146, because the number of steps is unchanged
1.5482, because a 40-step list is built and its last 21 values are kept
0.6708, because the list is built with 80 steps
questions.answer: 1.5482, because a 40-step list is built and its last 21 values are kept
questions.why: KSampler.set_steps builds a list with int(steps / denoise) steps and keeps the last steps + 1 values. The lab prints 1.5482 for denoise 0.5 and 0.6708 for denoise 0.25.

questions.q: In the toy run, x starts 38.975 from its final value and the denoised estimate 2.065. Which of the two does the sampling preview in ComfyUI show?
options: The noisy x
The denoised estimate
The average of the two
Neither, it renders the final image early
questions.why: The sampler passes the denoised latent to the preview callback, and latent_preview.py decodes that value. In the toy the estimate is far closer to the end result at the first step.

questions.q: How many network evaluations do 20 Euler steps and 20 Heun steps need in the lab?
options: 20 and 20
20 and 40
20 and 39
40 and 80
questions.why: Heun makes a second evaluation per step except on the last step, where the next sigma is 0 and it falls back to an Euler step. That gives 2 x 20 - 1 = 39.

questions.q: What happens to the negative prompt when the KSampler's cfg is exactly 1.0?
options: It is evaluated and then ignored
It is not evaluated, so each step needs one network call instead of two
It is added to the positive prompt
It raises an error
questions.answer: It is not evaluated, so each step needs one network call instead of two
questions.why: In sampling_function, a cond_scale close to 1.0 sets the unconditional input to None. With any other cfg the result is uncond + (cond - uncond) x cfg, which needs both predictions.
